newsitem.title: INDIA: India IDBI sanctions 20 bln rupee loans.
newsitem.headline: India IDBI sanctions 20 bln rupee loans.

text.p: The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) has sanctioned 20 billion rupees worth of long-term loans, a top IDBI official said on Friday.
About 70 percent of the loan sanctions, approved on Thursday, are for core infrastructure projects, he said.
The Economic Times on Friday, reporting the loan sanctions, described it as "the first clear signs of demand picking up on the project finance front."
"Today's sanctions are almost equal to those made by IDBI in the past three months and could well signal a reversal in (the recent poor) credit offtake," it said.
The Business Standard newspaper said the IDBI decided to reduce the spread of 25 to 75 basis points over its prime rate of 14.5 percent per annum on short-term loans.
An IDBI official told Reuters earlier this month that it earmarked only about 25 billion rupees for short-term loans during 1997/98 (April-March).
IDBI's focus continues to be on long-term loans, the official said. It is India's leading term lender.
